source.title: On some open problems of Radu

accepted.question_text: Let T be a triangular norm, meaning a binary operation on [0,1] that is commutative, monotone in both arguments, has T(a,1)=a, and is associative. Let (X,F,T) be a complete generalized Menger space, where Fxy is the probabilistic distance between x and y. For increasing functions alpha:[0,infinity)->[0,infinity) and beta:[0,1]->[0,1] with alpha(t)<=t, iterates of alpha tending to 0, beta(u)>=u, gamma(s)=max(alpha(s),1-beta(1-s)) continuous, and the iterated-control series for gamma finite for every s<1, consider a self-map A:X->X satisfying F_{A x,A y}(alpha(t)) >= beta(F_{x y}(t)) for all x,y in X and t>=0, with F_{x,A x}(u)>0 for some x in X and u>0. Which triangular norms T make this contraction principle guarantee that A has a fixed point on every complete generalized Menger space (X,F,T)?

In the same generalized probabilistic contraction setting, let alpha, beta, and gamma be the control functions used in the condition F_{f(x),f(y)}(alpha(t)) >= beta(F_{x,y}(t)), with gamma(s)=max(alpha(s),1-beta(1-s)). When the triangular norm T governing the Menger-space structure is replaced by an arbitrary Archimedean triangular norm, what conditions on alpha, beta, and gamma are appropriate to obtain a fixed point result?
